court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Judge, Family Court No.3, Mumbai, Petition No. A-121 of 2021
case_name: Bhairav Kumar Surajmal Jain vs Neeta Mithalal Jain
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed for divorce under Section 13(1)(i-a) and 13(1) (i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, on grounds of cruelty. Respondent claimed interim maintenance of Rs. 15,000/- per month.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party claiming maintenance to prove their income and expenses.
legal_principles.held: He further relies on the ITRs of the Respondent for the A.Y. 2017-18, which reflects her gross income of 2,83,698/- to contend that, payment of Income Tax Returns ('ITRs') itself is indicative of the fact that the Respondent has a source of income.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not grant maintenance to a party who has suppressed their actual income.
legal_principles.held: He further relies on the statement of account of the Respondent, of the Bharat Co-operative Bank Ltd.(Mumbai) to support his claim that, there are various entries of sizeable amounts deposited in the account of Respondent.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for interim maintenance in a Hindu marriage case
advising on the implications of Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act
assisting with a writ petition challenging an order of the Family Court
